questions.prompt: Why must binary files be opened with 'rb' or 'wb' modes rather than plain 'r' or 'w'?

options.text: To prevent the C runtime from performing automatic newline translations (CRLF vs LF) on Windows platforms
Binary mode compresses the data automatically
Standard C does not support plain 'r' mode

questions.explanation: Text mode on Windows translates \n into \r\n on write and vice-versa on read, corrupting raw binary structs.

questions.prompt: What is the primary role of a pthread_mutex_t in multi-threaded C?

options.text: To guarantee mutual exclusion and prevent race conditions on shared memory
To allocate heap memory for new threads

questions.explanation: A mutex ensures only one thread executes a critical section at any time, eliminating data races.
